paite: Ni nuai a ka muh gilou a-om a, mite tung ah agik hi.
heading: Hauhsakna Leh Haksatna
english: There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, and it is heavy on men:

paite: Mi Pathian in hauhsakna leh neih zohna leh zahna apiak a, huchi a adeih peuh akha a dia bangmah taksap nei het lou a, himahleh huai ne ding a Pathian in thilhihtheihna apiak louh a, mikhual in anek zawkna; hiai bangmah lou ahi a, gilou natna ahi.
english: a man to whom God gives riches, wealth, and honor, so that he lacks nothing for his soul of all that he desires, yet God gives him no power to eat of it, but an alien eats it. This is vanity, and it is an evil disease.

paite: Mihing in ta zakhat suang henla, kum tampi dam in akumte nite tampi phaleh, akha lah hoih in dim kei ngal in, kivuina nei kei ngalleh; amah a ding in ahun lou a pian ahoihzaw ka chi ahi.
english: If a man fathers a hundred children, and lives many years, so that the days of his years are many, but his soul is not filled with good, and moreover he has no burial, I say that a stillborn child is better than he;

paite: Bangmah lou lah ahong hi a, khomial ah apaimang a, khomial in amin akhuh hi.
english: for it comes in vanity, and departs in darkness, and its name is covered with darkness.

paite: Huai lou in ni amu kei a, theih leng athei kei; hiai in adang sang in akhawlna anei hi.
english: Moreover it has not seen the sun nor known it. This has rest rather than the other.

paite: Ahi, kum sangkhat gentuan dam mahleh, hoih nuam asakpih tuan kei; bang teng mun khat ah apai kei uh maw?
english: Yes, though he live a thousand years twice told, and yet fails to enjoy good, don’t all go to one place?

paite: Mihing sepgimna tengteng akam a ding ahi a, himahleh agilkialna adim tuan kei.
english: All the labor of man is for his mouth, and yet the appetite is not filled.

paite: Mihai sang in mipil in bang phattuamna anei a le? Ahihkeileh, mihing ma a omdan thei, migenthei in bang anei a?
english: For what advantage has the wise more than the fool? What has the poor man, that knows how to walk before the living?

paite: Lunggulhna tam vak sang in mitte muh ahoihzaw hi; hiai leng bangmah lou leh huih nungdelh lel ahi.
english: Better is the sight of the eyes than the wandering of the desire. This also is vanity and a chasing after wind.

paite: Ana om khinsa bangpeuh, sawtpi a huai amin piaksa ahi, huan mihing ahi chih theih ahi; amah sang a hatzaw amah toh leng akisual thei kei ding hi.
english: Whatever has been, its name was given long ago; and it is known what man is; neither can he contend with him who is mightier than he.

paite: Thil tampi bangmah lou pungsak a om ding chih thei in, mihing bang ahoih tuan a?
english: For there are many words that create vanity. What does that profit man?

paite: Adamsung bangmah lou limliap bang a asukbei tengteng, adamsung in mihing a ding a hoih kua'n athei a le? Ni nuai ah amah nung in bang a-om dia chih kua'n mihing ahilh thei a ahia?
english: For who knows what is good for man in life, all the days of his vain life which he spends like a shadow? For who can tell a man what will be after him under the sun?
